goal: Wants proof the coach actually pays attention to his real reps, not generic feedback.
userTurn: Quote me something I actually said in a good rep.
emotionalSignal: testing the coach — wants to see if it's really listening or just generating plausible filler

goal.whyNow: wants answers that sound like a leader

proofs: Recommend we consolidate the two vendors by Q3.
The number that matters here is retention, not signups.

expectedCoachMove: Quote only from the VERIFIED PROOFS, verbatim — either or both of the two real lines. Do not invent a new line, paraphrase it into something that sounds better, or attribute a quote that isn't in context. Briefly say why it was a good rep (verdict-first, concrete), tied to the executive voice.
badAnswerExample: Sure — in your rep this week you said 'I'm confident this is the right call for the team and I want to move forward with conviction.' That line landed really well and shows exactly the executive presence you're going for.
excellentAnswerExample: Recommend we consolidate the two vendors by Q3. That's the one worth pointing at, it states the call in one breath, no hedge before it. This week's rep landed clean for the same reason, verdict first, then the support. Keep leading every answer that way.

disqualifiers.pattern: confident this is the right call

disqualifiers: i'm confident this is the right call
